_comment: A6 / red-team item 6: the declared, reviewed exceptions battery_verdict.py measures every real check_all.sh run against. Every entry names its class, a reason, the date recorded, a review_by date and a removal_condition. An exception PAST its review_by turns blocking (a failure cemetery is not allowed), and one that starts PASSING shows up as 'recovered', so a stale entry rots visibly rather than normalizing a permanent known failure. TEST GRANULARITY, 2026-09-03: an entry for a check whose FAIL output names its failing tests declares them under failing_tests, one reason and removal condition per test name, because an exception keyed on the whole check shelters every future failure in it too. The verdict diffs the log's failing names against the declared set, and its own schema check (battery_verdict.py --check-expectations) refuses an entry that declares only a count or only a suite.

negative-space-audit.reason: R27.2's generated negative-space contract audit reports NO-DATA (exit 2) by design for every cell nobody has answered yet; these are the honest open findings the mechanism exists to surface, not a broken check.
negative-space-audit.removal_condition: the open negative-space cells are answered or reviewed-exempt so the audit exits 0; then delete this entry

wire-dual-principal.reason: VAULT-HARDENING-SCOPE-2026-08-31.md V3b: bm_vault_serve.py's served POST /recall reads no agent-shaped field (confirmed both statically, from its own source, and behaviorally, by sending every plausible spelling and observing no change in what is served); the CLI's VB3-04 dual-principal intersection guarantee (bm_vault_policy.decide_dual) is therefore unreachable at the buyer-facing HTTP boundary. scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py records this as FAIL-BY-DESIGN, a defect record naming the gap, never new capability built to close it.
wire-dual-principal.removal_condition: the served /recall endpoint gains a second principal field (for example agent_identity) and applies decide_dual's intersection semantics at the wire, proven by scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py exiting 0; then delete this entry
wire-dual-principal.failing_tests: none: the battery runs scripts/test_wire_dual_principal.py's main() probe, which prints one CAN or CANNOT verdict and exits 1 by design (FAIL-BY-DESIGN); its unittest class runs only under --unittest, so the check's output names no failing tests

product-brothermode.reason: RE-MEASURED 2026-09-03 AT TEST GRANULARITY, applying the estate's own lesson that a suite-level exception hides every new failure in the suite. WHAT THE OLD ENTRY DID: it declared this check as a whole and named three tests in prose, while battery round 11 (commit 8f9f9968) read test_bm_docs.py FAILED (failures=10, skipped=4) plus test_brothermode_cli.py FAILED (failures=1). Reproduced on that same saved log: the pre-change verdict exits 0 and lists product-brothermode under expected_unavailable, so eight undeclared failures, two of them about release identity, rode a green release verdict. TEN OF THE ELEVEN ARE NOW FIXED, NOT DECLARED, on two root causes. (1) EIGHT test_bm_docs names came from one half-moved fact: commit 57ad2135 (row E32) moved .claude-plugin/plugin.json's repository field to the hub because that is the repository the marketplace installs the plugin from, and scripts/test_version_truth.py now fails a subtree whose repository field disagrees with its marketplace source, while product.identity.json still carried one repo_url that the identity-manifests comparison held equal to BOTH plugin.json fields. The product's own verify-docs entry point therefore failed its identity-manifests lane on the real tree and on every fixture built from it. Fixed by splitting the two facts rather than by moving the one that is still true: product.identity.json carries ships_from_url (the hub the plugin installs from) beside repo_url (this product's own repository, which owns the tags an auditor clones and which plugin.json's homepage names), and both readers of that comparison, tools/bm_docs.py's identity_manifest_offenders and the suite's own copy, read the ship-from fact for the repository field. (2) ONE came from a tag assumption that two tests in this same file disagreed about: test_the_primary_install_command_uses_the_tag_not_a_branch asserted the install pages pin release_tag (v plus VERSION) while TestOneInstall.test_the_pinned_install_uses_the_public_install_target_tag asserts, and has always asserted, install_target_tag, the tag known to actually resolve. The two agreed only while the two facts happened to be equal, which the M6 cutover ended: 3.4.4 ships at the hub's own tag v0.9.11 (CHANGELOG.md, .claude-plugin/marketplace.json), no tag named v3.4.4 is ever cut, and the install pages are right to keep pinning v3.4.2. The first test now reads install_target_tag and keeps the half it uniquely owns, that the pin exists and is not the moving default branch. (3) ONE was a documentation gap, and its first fix introduced an eleventh failure that is also fixed here, which is why the two measurements name different tenth tests: round 11 failed test_release_md_states_the_current_version because docs/RELEASE.md carried no entry for the two hub-era cuts, and the entry written for it spelled the archived repository's slug in prose, where the identity contract allows it only inside a code region, so test_no_current_page_uses_a_retired_name_as_the_product_name then failed on docs/RELEASE.md:657. The page now records 3.4.4 and the hub tag it shipped under, with the slug in a code span, and both tests pass. Measured after the last edit in this tree: test_bm_docs.py 241 tests OK (skipped=4), and tools/test_all.py reads 5314 tests across 130 suites, 16 skipped, 1 SUITE(S) FAILED, down from 2 suites and 11 failing tests. WHAT REMAINS is the one name below, and it is machine state rather than code. The previous entry's own count had already come down from three suites to two on the night of 2026-09-02, when a pyproject.toml version defect and a decision record's status line were found to be real defects and fixed.
product-brothermode.removal_condition: delete the one name below the battery after it reads recovered, and delete this entry with it. Nothing else is sheltered here: the ten other failures this entry used to cover were fixed on 2026-09-03 rather than declared, so a new failing name in either suite is an unexpected failure and blocks, which is the whole point of naming them.

test_doctor_reports_only_expected_failur.reason: MACHINE STATE, NOT CODE, and the test says so in its own comment: it runs its assertion only where doctor's consent check PASSES, meaning BrotherMode is actually installed on the machine running it, and it allows doctor to be red mid-train on check 11 (the CHECKSUMS manifest) alone. Seen failing in this tree on 2026-09-03 after the manifest was rebuilt, verbatim: 'AssertionError: Lists differ: [1, 10] != [11] : doctor may only be red mid-train on the manifest check; any other FAIL is real: [1, 10]'. Check 1 is fence ('NO FENCE HOOK IS WIRED. settings.json ... has no PreToolUse entry naming bm_fence_hook.py') and check 10 is mode_wiring ('installation_mode is clone but no BrotherMode hook wiring was found'). Both are doctor telling the exact truth about THIS machine, which runs the marketplace plugin while this checkout's installation_mode reads clone, so no clone hook wiring exists in settings.json to find. Asserting them away would be asserting a falsehood, and the product's doctor passes where the product is installed the way its own config says it is.
test_doctor_reports_only_expected_failur.removal_condition: this machine's installation_mode is reconciled with how the plugin is actually installed (python3 scripts/install.py, or an installation_mode that names the marketplace install), and doctor reads checks 1 and 10 PASS; then this name is deleted and the entry with it.

pre-push-gate.reason: E31, found by battery round 6: the estate certifies commits by running the battery on a git worktree pinned at one SHA, whose HEAD is detached. A detached head has no branch and no outgoing range, so scripts/pre_push_gate.py's correctness check reads NO-DATA there by design; nothing pushes from a pinned worktree. On the checkout that actually pushes, the same check reads PASS or a real refusal, and a genuine FAIL there still blocks: this declaration covers only the pinned-worktree NO-DATA, never a FAIL.
pre-push-gate.removal_condition: structural, not a defect: a worktree pinned at one SHA carries a detached HEAD by construction, so pre-push-gate reads NO-DATA there for as long as certification runs against pinned worktrees. Remove this entry only if that workflow stops using detached checkouts, or pre_push_gate.py is redesigned to give a verdict there some other way

product-brothersbe-tests.reason: E33 registered products/brothersbe/tools/test_sbe.py in the battery on 2026-09-03. The file reads OK (skipped=2) and one skip's own reason says NO-DATA: TestTheUpdateNoticeIsUnconditional reads the sibling BrotherModeUp's real source only when it is installed at the legacy skills path (~/.claude/skills/brothermode/tools/bm_telemetry.py), and on this machine the sibling is installed as a plugin, not at that path. The battery's rule counts a skip whose reason says NO-DATA as NO-DATA, which is right; this declaration records that it is machine-bound. A FAIL under this declaration still blocks.
product-brothersbe-tests.removal_condition: the test resolves the sibling through the plugin install path as well as the legacy skills path, or the skip is rewritten to read the installed plugin's copy; then the line reads PASS (recovered) and this entry is deleted

test_this_repository_passes_its_own_root.reason: reads red since PR 88 (2026-09-04 00:0x JST) minted design, gate and score receipts for the estate's own dossiers: the assurance product reads a receipt as stale once any later commit lands (row E83, the receipt freshness defects: a dossier-scoped status never lets a receipt exempt itself and a sibling receipt's commit invalidates the others), so gate --strict over the repository root fails on its own receipts. Being fixed in the founder's separate session (E83).
test_this_repository_passes_its_own_root.removal_condition: E83 lands and bin/sbe gate --strict over the repository root reads PASS on the minted receipts; then delete this test entry

repair-drain-self.reason: Registered in the battery for the first time 2026-09-04 (QA reviewer finding 3, 107 unrun checkers). scripts/test_repair_drain.py's own second-attempt scenario now collides with a rule that landed after this test was written: receipt_door.py's 'the check already passed before the work' handling (memory: a-check-that-already-passes-before-the-work-proves-nothing.md). test_second_attempt_repairs_after_a_failed_first drives brother_run through a failing first attempt and a repairing second attempt, and asserts the second attempt exits 0 (PASS). Because the fixture's check already reads true before the second attempt's own work runs, brother_run now correctly refuses to credit it as a proof and reports the piece NO-DATA instead, so the run exits 2, not 0, verbatim: 'brother_run: exit 2: nothing in this run was verified (0 PASS, 1 NO-DATA); a run that refused nothing but proved nothing is not the same thing as success' and 'F1 is NO-DATA: the check already passed before the work began, so it cannot prove the work.' This is the newer rule working as designed against an older test's assumption, not a product regression; the test's assertion is stale, not the code, and is left failing rather than weakened per this estate's rule that a failing test is never softened to get green.
repair-drain-self.removal_condition: test_second_attempt_repairs_after_a_failed_first's fixture is rewritten so the second attempt's check is not already-true before the work runs (or the test's own expected exit code is updated to 2/NO-DATA to match the now-correct already-passed rule), and scripts/test_repair_drain.py exits 0; then this entry is deleted

test_second_attempt_repairs_after_a_fail.reason: AssertionError: 2 != 0, because the second attempt's check already reads true before that attempt's own work runs, so receipt_door.py scores it NO-DATA ('the check already passed before the work began, so it cannot prove the work') rather than PASS, and brother_run exits 2. The test predates this rule and still asserts exit 0.
test_second_attempt_repairs_after_a_fail.removal_condition: the fixture is changed so the second attempt's check is genuinely false until the repair lands (a true proof), or the test is updated to assert the NO-DATA/exit-2 verdict this rule now produces; then scripts/test_repair_drain.py exits 0 and this name is deleted with it

product-brothersbe-battery.reason: NARROWED 2026-09-04 (row E82, lane BI2). The entry previously declared three failing steps: 05-honesty-meta, 05b-honesty-seeded and 35-upgrade-rollback. All three are now fixed at the root and read exit=0. 05-honesty-meta and 05b-honesty-seeded: the residual was fifteen helper functions across eight tools/ files that evals/test_no_data_class.py's inverted verdict-source lint flagged as 'can return the verdict PASS but sit in no registry'. Each of the fifteen was read individually; none forms, alters or forwards a verdict. They are three shapes only, the same three every pre-existing allowlist entry belongs to: a parser or reader returning (value, problems), a subprocess or captured-output wrapper returning (exit code, combined output) where any verdict word in that text belongs to the tool under test, and one fixture builder returning (path, path). Each was added to that file's own NOT_A_VERDICT allowlist with a reason naming its return shape, which is the lint's designed and reconciled escape hatch: an entry naming no function fails, and an entry resolving to two functions of that name fails, so the exemption binds to the body that was reviewed. No lint rule was loosened and no helper was rewritten to satisfy the scanner. 35-upgrade-rollback: products/brothersbe/scripts/test-upgrade-rollback.sh selected the newest ancestor tag matching 'v[0-9]*' as 'the previous release of this product', but that family is the HUB's umbrella tags, shared across the monorepo. It picked v0.9.6, a hub release that predates products/brothersbe/ existing in the tree, and then failed because scripts/verify-install.sh 'did not ship' in it, which is a true statement about a tree that was never this product's release. The selection now matches the estate's documented per-product tag form, 'brothersbe--v[0-9]*' (two dashes; products/brothermode/docs/plan/ADR-2026-08-23-one-brother-repository.md), and no such tag has been cut in the hub yet, so the script prints NO-DATA naming exactly what it looked for and what it deliberately ignored, and exits 0 without claiming an upgrade was tested. Driven BOTH ways rather than only to green: with a throwaway local brothersbe--v tag on an ancestor commit the script selected it, installed the previous release, HEAD and the rollback, verified all three clean and printed PASSED; the tag was then deleted. WHAT STILL FAILS, and it is not one of this row's original eight: 01-hard-gates and 06-tool-tests read FAIL because design/*/.sbe/evidence ran-receipts are pinned to a commit main has moved past. That is row E83 (the receipt freshness defects: a dossier-scoped status never lets a receipt exempt itself, and a sibling receipt's commit invalidates the others), owned by a separate session. The battery wrapper greps its own summary.txt for any non-zero exit, so this check line stays FAIL for as long as those two steps do.
product-brothersbe-battery.removal_condition: E83 lands and 01-hard-gates and 06-tool-tests read exit=0 in a fresh release-control/baseline/run-battery.sh run; then this entry is deleted. No other step is sheltered by it: a non-zero exit from any of the other 92 steps blocks.
product-brothersbe-battery.failing_tests: none: this check wraps release-control/baseline/run-battery.sh, a 94-step shell battery, not a single unittest suite, so its own output names step numbers rather than unittest test names. The two steps still non-zero are 01-hard-gates (python3 tools/sbe_gate.py --strict design) and 06-tool-tests (python3 tools/test_sbe.py), both on the E83 stale-receipt class. Every one of this row's original eight steps now reads exit=0.
